title: FLORA CITY COUNCIL MEETS
full_story:
The Flora City Council met on Monday afternoon, beginning with a pair of public hearings.  The first was concerning rezoning property along South Stanford Road from agricultural (A-2) to MF-1 to allow for multi-family dwellings.  The designation is sought by the developer Ruth Street Apartments.  With no comment, the hearing ended and the second public hearing got underway.  The budget hearing gave the public an opportunity to voice their opinions about the proposed 2026-27 Budget for the City of Flora.  City leaders presented a budget summary which shows the budget, including pooled cash, debt service, separate and restricted accounts have an estimated income of $39,017,223.  With over $4,000,000 of the budget coming from grants that the city has been able to secure for capital projects within the City of Flora.  These range from building improvements, roads, sidewalks, infrastructure improvements and quality of life improvements in parks.  The operating expenses for the 2026-27 budget is $38,375,557.  The pooled cash account budget is $27,393,941.  There are 18 accounts that make up the Pooled Cash Account the Pooled Cash makes up 76% of the overall budget.    The budget is available for public inspection at Flora City Hall.  With no public comment, the hearing ended and the regular meeting began when Mayor Linda Spicer called the meeting to order.

With no visitors seeking to speak to commissioners, the group quickly approved the meeting agenda and the consent agenda.  The latter included past meeting minutes, the warrant list, the Police Activity Report, the Building and Zoning Report and the Treasurer’s Report.

In Regular Business, Mayor Spicer commented on the retirement of K9 Officer Hektor who was partnered with Flora Police Officer Aaron Holman.  The mayor wished Hektor well in his retirement and welcomed new K9 Officer Duke who is paired with Flora Police Officer Luke Durre.  The mayor then called on commissioners for their comments.  Commissioner Phil Wiley mentioned that Flora High School’s Prom is this Saturday and urged everyone to be safe in their celebrations and for others who may have interactions with them.  Wiley also made a motion to suspend the annual electric rate increase until the rate study is completed.  That measure was seconded and commissioners approved it unanimously.

Next, Flora City Administrator/Economic Development Director Mike Stanford presented two items for commissioners’ consideration.  He asked the council to approve the renewal of it’s Symetra Policy for city employees that includes a 6% increase.  That puts the rate for a single person at $426.36 and a family rate of $959.26. The measure was approved without dissent.  Stanford then moved on to request a 3% increase for health insurance premiums for city employees, pointing out that this is just the 2nd increase in premiums in nine years.  Stanford closed by noting the health coverage is self-funded and is adequate and is in good shape.

The meeting moved on to Treasurer Stephanie Bailey, who presented three action items for the council.  First was an ordinance to adopt the city’s FY2026/27 Budget, which commissioners approve unanimously.  Members then approved an ordinance amending the FY2025/26 Budget.  Bailey closed with a request for an $18,000 increase to the Tyler Technologies contract.  The increase is for a software upgrade to Cloud Based Utility Billing, Meter Interface, Cashiering Storage, Time Keeping, Payroll Interface and Accounts Payable.  Following an endorsement by Commissioner Wiley, the measure was approved unanimously.

Building and Zoning Official Chad Bayles was absent, however in his place City Administrator Mike Stanford sought commissioners’ approval.  Up first was the subject of the public hearing on rezoning.  Stanford explained the request from the developer is to rezone the area for the Ruth Street Apartments just off South Stanford Road from Agriculture A-2 to Multi-Family MF-1.  It was approved unanimously.  Next was an ordinance granting a variance to a trust agreement from February 2, 1981, for the property at 509 N. State Street.  Commissioners approved the measure.  It will become the site for Flora resident Jeff Yates’ Landscaping business, which he tells WNOI that it will likely be next Fall before much happens to the property.  The final item of the meeting was an ordinance amending Title 4, Chapter 1, Section 1 Adoption of Building Code, which was requested by the state to be known as the Illinois Energy Conservation Code.  The measure was approved and the meeting adjourned.

title: FLORA BUILDING AND ZONING REPORT
full_story:
In Flora Building and Zoning Official Chad Bayles absence, Flora City Administrator presented the monthly building and zoning report for March during Monday’s Flora City Council meeting.

The report shows 6 new residential Construction projects were undertaken in March, valued at $77,500.

There was 1 new commercial project started during March, valued at $40,000.

And there were no new industrial projects started during March.

There were 7 total new projects in Flora for March, valued at $117,500 with $318 collected in permit fees and $50 in deposit fees for March

The year-to-date figures show 15 total residential projects so far this year with a value of $154,864.

There is one year-to-date commercial project valued at $40,000 and no new industrial projects.

That makes for a total of 19 total projects valued at $194,864, with $723 in permit fees and $200 in deposit fees collected.

title: FLORA POLICE ACTIVITY REPORT
full_story:
Flora Chief of Jeremy Ruger released his Activity Report for March during Monday’s Flora City Council meeting.

During the month, Flora police officers investigated 6 traffic accidents.

They made 7 criminal arrests.  There were no drug arrets and 1 DUI arrest during March.  There were 4 local ordinance arrests, 11 traffic arrests and 5 warrant arrests.

Officers issued 55 warning tickets, responded to 20 alarms and had 1,238 calls for service and had no juvenile contacts.

Also, Flora police officers drove 7,312 miles and conducted 73 investigations during March.  They answered 343, 911 calls and conducted 15 UTV Inspections and no Golf Cart Inspections during March.

title: DRUG TAKE BACK DAY
full_story:
The Clay County Hospital will be the drop off location for the Clay County prescription drug take-back initiative on Saturday, from 10 am to 1 pm.

The National Prescription Drug Take Back Day aims to provide a safe, convenient, and responsible means of disposing of prescription drugs, while also educating the general public about the potential for abuse of medications.

Unused medications in the home are a source of drug abuse in millions of homes, 80% of US waterways show traces of common medication; and 56% of teens think that prescription drugs are easier to get than illicit drugs.

The Drug Take Back Day will provide a safe and trusted method of disposal of prescription drugs.

The drug take back event on Saturday, is sponsored by the Coalition Against Drug Abuse of Clay County in cooperation with the Clay County Sheriff’s Office, Flora Police Department, Clay County Hospital, Clay County Solid Waste Committee, Clay County Health Department, and Clay County Probation.

title: FROG ISLAND TENNIS CAMP
full_story:
Flora High School Tennis Coach Daniel Pieplow has announced that the Frog Island Tennis Camp will run Monday, June 1st through Friday, June 5th at the Kayo Powless Tennis Courts.

This year incoming 9th through 12th graders will have camp from 8:30 to 9:30 am; 2nd through 5th grade will have camp from 9:30 to 10:30, and incoming 6th through 8th graders will have camp from 10:30 to 11:30 am.

title: HONOR FLIGHT MISSION 77
full_story:
Land of Lincoln Honor Flight will be taking Mission #77 on May 5th.

Mission #77 will serve 95 veterans, 5 Korean and 90 Vietnam Era Veterans from 54 Illinois hometowns representing all branches of the military.

These Veterans and their Guardians will report Tuesday, May 5th, to the Abraham Lincoln Capitol Airport at 4:00 AM to travel to Washington DC to visit the World War II, Korean and Vietnam War Memorials, as well as Arlington National Cemetery Tomb of the Unknowns, the Lincoln Memorial, the National Air & Space Museum in Chantilly, Virginia, the US Marine Corps Memorial and the US Air Force Memorial.  This day of honor is provided at absolutely no cost to veterans and is completely funded by donations from the general public.

These 95 heroes will return to the Springfield airport at 9:30 PM on Tuesday May 5th.  The general public, friends, family and LLHF alumni veterans are encouraged to pack the airport to welcome home these heroes.  Greeters are encouraged to arrive early and show appreciation for and support of these veterans who sacrificed so much for our country.  Parking is free and volunteers will be in the parking area to assist guests to open spaces.  A shuttle bus is available to take guests directly to the airport terminal door.

Any veteran who served at any time up through May 7th of 1975 is eligible to participate, regardless of where they served or their assigned duties.  Any seriously impaired or terminally ill WWII, Korean era or Vietnam era veteran will be given flight priority.  Veteran and Guardian Applications can be obtained at www.LandofLincolnHonorFlight.org by clicking on “Applications” tab.  LLHF also offers a “Flightless Honor Flight” program for those otherwise eligible veterans whose physical condition limits their ability to participate on an actual flight.

Land of Lincoln Honor Flight is a 501(c)3 non-profit organization that receives no government funding.  Over 6,000 Central Illinois veterans have been served on LLHF’s 75 flights.  It is only able to honor veterans due to the generous donations, sponsorships, fundraising events, merchandise sales and supporting efforts of the many local businesses, individuals, and organizations within the service area.  Land of Lincoln Honor Flight is operated by all volunteers; it has no paid staff, no rental, and no utilities costs.

title: HOSTS STILL NEEDED
full_story:
Several state parks and historic sites operated by the Illinois Department of Natural Resources (IDNR) are still seeking campground hosts for the 2026 season.

Sites in Southern Illinois actively searching for campground hosts include; Wayne Fitzgerrell State Recreation Area at Rend Lake in Franklin County, Giant City State Park in Jackson County, Cave-in-Rock State Park in Hardin County, Stephen A. Forbes State Recreation Area in Marion County, World Shooting and Recreational Complex in Randolph County, and Saline County State Fish and Wildlife Area.

Campground hosting is a perfect position for anyone who enjoys camping and helping others.  Hosts are often the first to greet state park visitors.  They check on arrivals and departures, write camping permits, acquaint campers with park facilities and regulations, answer questions about local and statewide attractions, help visitors plan outings and more.

Hosts have the privilege of free camping in their own RVs, motorhomes, or trailers at designated sites within state parks.  Anyone interested in being a campground host can complete and submit a campground host program packet at the desired site.  Questions can be directed to the superintendent at the appropriate site.
